# Mimetic desire

The claim: desire is not a straight line from a person to an object. It is a triangle. We want what a model wants, and we want it because the model wants it. Imitation comes first and the object second.

## The triangle

Subject, model, object. The model can be distant (a figure we will never meet) or close (a colleague, a sibling, a neighbour). When the model is distant the imitation is harmless, because we never compete for the same object.

## Rivalry

When the model is close, imitation turns into rivalry. Two people who imitate each other's desire converge on the same object and each reads the other's wanting as proof that the object is worth having. The rivalry feeds itself: the more one side wants, the more the other does. At the limit the object drops away and only the rivals remain, fascinated by each other. ^rivalry-def

## Contagion

In a crowd the same mechanism spreads sideways. Each person imitates the people nearby, the wanting synchronises, and the crowd converges on one object or one enemy. This is why collective enthusiasm and collective panic look so alike.

Related: [[Desire as lack]], [[Positional goods]].
